question: State the fundamental principle of counting. Distinguish between a permutation and a combination, and show how the two are related.
sources: Permutations and combinations (standard principles of counting)

points.label: Fundamental principle of counting
points.description: If one operation can be done in m ways and, after it, a second in n ways, both together can be done in m × n ways (multiplication rule); if they are alternatives that cannot happen together, either can be done in m + n ways (addition rule).

points.label: Permutation
points.description: A permutation is an arrangement of objects in which order matters; the number of permutations of n different things taken r at a time is n!/(n − r)!.

points.label: Combination
points.description: A combination is a selection of objects in which order does not matter; the number of combinations of n different things taken r at a time is n!/[r!(n − r)!].

points.label: Relation and example
points.description: Each combination of r things can be arranged in r! ways, so nPr = r! × nCr; for example, choosing 2 of 3 people for a team is a combination (3 ways), while choosing a captain and vice-captain is a permutation (6 ways).
